app/src/routes/index.js:86,99, app/src/routes/moves/[name].js:58,69, app/src/routes/abilities/[name].js:46,57, app/src/routes/types/[name].js:64,75, app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].js:209,220 — the Map→Object→Map typeNames round-trip boilerplate is repeated in all five routes

app/src/routes/index.client.js:31-38, app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].client.js:15-24 — client enhancements are cleanly separated: they import no server modules and couple only via element ids (#results, #moves-tables) and query params

coupling.rationale: Server/client separation and the lib layering are genuinely good, but pokemonCard's typeNames Map parameter is a leak that forces every card-list handler (current and future) to fetch and thread data it doesn't need, and the media-URL knowledge sits in the wrong layer.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.js:57-77 — pokemonRefsToSpecies(refs, extraOf) captures the real variation across three pages (alternate-form exclusion, species dedup, dex ordering, per-caller extra payload) without flag parameters
app/src/lib/views.js:14-46 — pokemonCard takes an options object (types/note) instead of booleans, covering the home page's badges and abilities' hidden-ability note in one component

app/src/routes/*/​*.js (7 sites, e.g. app/src/routes/types/index.js:35) — 'document: (context) => document({...context, title: context.props.GET.title})' wiring and the '${enName} – Pokédex' title pattern are repeated in every route instead of centralized in document.js
app/src/document.js:3 — a single layout seam that all pages share, correctly parameterized on title only
abstraction_design.rationale: The core abstractions (card rendering, ref→species resolution, layout, pure formatters) stretch to new cases well and avoid flag creep; the cost is copy-paste at the route-skeleton level, which is conventional in Gracile but adds real duplication for the next similar resource.

findings.issue: The production build output sits in the source tree and is not gitignored (root .gitignore only covers /data/, /.data-cache/, node_modules/), so every grep/find hits stale compiled duplicates of your own source (e.g. dist/server/chunk/_name_3.js:152 mirroring app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].js) and a 'git add .' would commit generated code that will rot.
findings.suggestion: Add 'app/dist/' (or 'dist/') to .gitignore and rely on 'npm run build' before 'npm start', as package.json already specifies.

findings.issue: The handler fetches and serializes all 18 type resources solely to satisfy pokemonCard's typeNames parameter, which this page never renders (its cards have no type badges); every future card-list page inherits this needless fetch-and-thread.
findings.suggestion: Make typeNames an optional third argument (default null) and short-circuit in pokemonCard when no types are requested, or resolve type labels inside a shared typeName() helper so routes never pass the Map.

findings.issue: The filter query-string encoding rules (omit empty values, omit page at 1) are duplicated between the server's pagination link builder and the client's currentUrl(); adding or renaming a filter parameter must be done twice or the two views of the URL drift.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared buildListUrl(params) pure function into app/src/lib/ (client route files can import plain JS) and use it from both the route template and the client script.

findings.issue: The media URL layout (/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png) and the API base are knowledge of the data source, but they live in the view layer, so changing where media is served means editing a template module.
findings.suggestion: Move spriteUrl into app/src/lib/api.js (or data.js) next to base(), keeping views.js free of transport details.

findings.location: app/src/routes/moves/[name].js:26-28,58-60 (same pattern in abilities, types, pokemon, index)
findings.issue: The resource-page skeleton — 404 branch (status + notFound props), '${enName} – Pokédex' title assembly and the document wiring — is copy-pasted across five routes; an Items page would clone it a sixth time.
findings.suggestion: Add tiny helpers: notFoundProps() in lib/views.js and a title-computing document wrapper (or compute the title inside document.js from props), so new routes share them.

findings.issue: The cache-a-promo-them/evict-on-error mechanics are written twice (api() and apiList()); introducing TTLs, key prefixes or invalidation means editing both implementations.
findings.suggestion: Factor a single memoize(path, loader) helper used by both functions so caching rules live in one place.

findings.issue: The option() helper is duplicated verbatim in two route files.
findings.suggestion: Move it to app/src/lib/views.js next to the other markup helpers.

findings.issue: The Map→Object.fromEntries→new Map(Object.entries()) round-trip for typeNames is repeated in every route because props must be serializable, adding boilerplate to each handler/template pair.
findings.suggestion: Standardize on a serializable shape (array of [name, label] pairs) with a small toTypeNames() helper, or drop the threading entirely per the pokemonCard fix above.

findings.issue: Feature-scoped selectors (.ability-list) in one global stylesheet mean removing a feature leaves dead CSS unless someone greps for the class names.
findings.suggestion: Keep the section comments (they help), but group feature styles under clearly-named banners, or consider Gracile's per-route CSS imports so styles travel with their route.

findings.issue: pokemonCard's options.note exists for exactly one caller (abilities' 'Hidden ability'); after removal of that feature the parameter becomes dead generality in a shared component.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is for one option; if more per-card variants appear, prefer composing a small slot/append function over growing the options object.

summary: A well-layered, idiomatic Gracile app that is easy to change at the bottom and only moderately so at the top: transport, domain shaping, formatting and shared markup each live in one module, and every card list funnels through a single pokemonCard seam, so the sprite bug is a one-line fix. The main debts are pokemonCard's typeNames Map leaking into every handler, duplicated filter-URL serialization across the server/client boundary, copy-pasted route skeletons, and unignored build output polluting the tree. I'd approve with the first four findings addressed.
